Data Validation
---

---

**Any data generated by this codebase currently has SMALL CATALOGUE data validation.<br>**
**It remains to run the code on the full catalogue.**

---

**Step 1: Model Validation (PASS)**<br>
In this step, we first generate a "truth" dataset based on the contrasts from previous work.<br>
Afterward, several models are created, the first one receiving the full dataset, the second half and the final one a 
quarter. <br>
If the mathematical foundations are enough, there should be no extreme deviation in any of the resulting contrasts.

Should the values be close to the truth even if not "trained" on the full dataset, this is a central indication 
that the model has converged to its optimal solution. Choosing higher resolutions will then eventually lead to a 
plateau in accuracy, which constitutes the absolute limit of the chosen mathematical model.


**Step 2: Full Data Validation (SMALL CATALOGUE PASS)**<br>
We implement the entirety of this codebase in LIFEsim. Yields are then run. They must be comparable to the yields
generated by the unmodified LIFEsim, especially regarding emerging patterns. Should this not be the case even though 
Step 1 was passed, an indication of a mistake in the physical simulation process of the contrast ratio, 
i.e., a deep bug is present.

---

**Details**
---

**Model Validation**

I. Model Interpolation Performance.
- FULL model (MAX, MIN, AVG, EXC) (OoM): $(0.78, -1.64, -0.43, 6.71\%)$
- HALF model (MAX, MIN, AVG, EXC) (OoM): $(0.83, -1.77, -0.42, 7.11\%)$
- QUARTER model (MAX, MIN, AVG, EXC) (OoM): $(0.82, -2.09, -0.48, 11.03\%)$

The performance here is given in deviation orders of magnitude (OoM), with the exceedance (EXC) being the percentage of 
data points with more than one order of magnitude deviation from the truth values.

II. Case Example: the sun at 10pc, integrated over wavelength.<br>
- Truth Contrast: $5.843717033496687 \times 10^{-10}$
- FULL model: $5.462766553300787 \times 10^{-10}$
- HALF model: $5.655197396936292 \times 10^{-10}$
- QUARTER model: $5.146697710750692 \times 10^{-10}$


We may conclude that a resolution of 40x40x40 is already close to reaching a plateau. Further tests with a resolution
of 80x80x80 have confirmed this theory and define the plateau as an exceedance of about 6%. 

Even in the case of the quarter model, the exceedance is only of order 10%, with the full computation time being about
two seconds.

This validation step has been passed.

---

**Full Data Validation**

Validation on a limited catalogue is completed. After full integration, the yields on the entire catalogue deviate by
0.59% (model / conventional), which signifies a science goal uncertainty of $30 \times 5.9 \times 10^{-3} = 0.18$ planets for a detection goal
of 30 samples.
